MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  APRIL 26, 2016

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:05 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Direct Andy Clark
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

Others Present:  Lou Persichina, Park and Activities Commission
  Tim Scott, Planning Commission
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineer

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

  NONE

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 12, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 12,
  2016 AS PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 12, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN  MITCHELL  requested  a  correction  under  Item  12B,
  Paragraph 6:

  “…Finally, he was pleased to note that the City of Palos Verdes Estates Policy
  Police Department is also participating in this program.”

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN requested a correction under Item 4B,
  Paragraph 2:

  “MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN ZUCKERMAN presented Raffy Mardirossian,
  Chair, Lomita Chapter of the South Bay Armenian Community Center with
  a Proclamation.”

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 12, 2016 AS
  AMENDED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
APRIL 26, 2016
 C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – APRIL

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 56701 THROUGH 56741 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $282,797.77 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)\

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NOS. A-C.

A.  MARCH 2016 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

B.  MARCH MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  LEGISLATIVE UPDATE

  DIRECTED STAFF TO TAKE THE POSITIONS AS LISTED BY THE LEAGUE
  OF CALIFORNIA CITIES, AND COMMUNICATE THE CITY’S POSITION
  WHEN AND WHERE APPROPRIATE.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, City Manager Prichard explained the
  policy that the COUNCIL follows in regards to the League of California Cities’
  various positions.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  LETTER FROM MASONGATE AND MARLOMA HOMEOWNERS’ ASSOCIATIONS
  REGARDING RECENTLY INSTALLED MEDIANS BETWEEN MASONGATE DRIVE
  AND MARLOMA DRIVE

  Jeanette Vanamburgh, President, Masongate Homeowners’ Association, referred
  to their letter requesting landscaping in the medians on Palos Verdes Drive North
  west of Hawthorne Boulevard.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL inquired if funding is available in the budget.
  Community Services Director Clark noted that this item is not budgeted.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that drought tolerant landscaping should be
  considered in the City’s medians.

  Following comments by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN regarding a comprehensive
  approach to the question of median landscaping, COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL
  suggested referring this item to the Park and Activities Commission.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to have the Park and
  Activities Commission discuss this matter and make a recommendation.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

  NONE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 26, 2016
 9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 18,
  2016

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 18, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL referred to the Rotary Club’s Beer and Wine Testing
  Festival at Ernie Howlett Park scheduled for May 15. She noted that the Palos
  Verdes Peninsula Chamber’s Economic Development Committee also supported
  this event.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL further noted that the Chamber is planning a
  “Dine Around the Peninsula Restaurant Week” on July 15-24 for those businesses
  who are members of the Chamber.

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  AUDIO VISUAL/BROADCAST SYSTEMS UPGRADE

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the solicitation of bids for
  the Audio Visual and Broadcast Systems Upgrade Project using the Audio
  Visual Master Plan Design pending final review and approval of the contract
  and bid documents by the City Attorney.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per
  agenda material).

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted that he will be supervising the project which should take place
  over the summer.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ inquired if there would be any disruption to
  COUNCIL meetings when this work takes place. Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead stated that there may be some down time associated with
  updating the technology in the Council Chambers.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead stated that the screen display will be shown for the audience behind
  the COUNCIL.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead noted that there are many options regarding the live feed of the
  COUNCIL meetings.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AUTHORIZE THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE AUDIO VISUAL
  AND BROADCAST SYSTEMS UPGRADE PROJECT USING THE AUDIO
  VISUAL MASTER PLAN DESIGN PENDING FINAL REVIEW AND
  APPROVAL OF THE CONTRACT AND BID DOCUMENTS BY THE CITY
  ATTORNEY.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL TEAMBUILDING WORKSHOP

  Recommendation:  That the City Council schedule a Teambuilding and
  Communication Workshop using the California Joint Powers Insurance
  Authority and identify what, if any, staff members should participate.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 26, 2016
   Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that this item was discussed at the Policy
  Development Session.

  Extensive discussion took place regarding the need, focus format and the cost
  of the proposed session along with the experience of the proposed facilitator and
  other options for reinforcing the organization’s culture, policies and procedures.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO CREATE A CURRICULUM BRING BACK
  RECOMMENDATIONS  TO  THE  COUNCIL  FOR  FURTHER
  CONSIDERATION.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 6, 2016 – MAYOR
  ZUCKERMAN

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  MINUTES OF APRIL 6, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF APRIL 6,
  2016: PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AT EASTVALE ROAD – REQUEST FOR
  EQUESTRIAN CROSSING

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the recommendations as
  listed in the staff report.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that the Equestrian Committee was
  unanimous in its opinion that providing a crossing on Palos Verdes Drive North
  at Eastvale Road was not a viable solution due to traffic and that removing the
  bushes and cleaning up the trail along the south side of Palos Verdes Drive
  North to provide a midblock crossing further east would be preferred.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL referred to the removal of the Pepper Trees.
  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that those particular trees are decayed
  and previously marked for removal, but will be replaced with additional trees at
  suitable locations.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that the trail would be 8-10 feet wide
  once the vegetation is cleared.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented on his concern with the bike lane
  along Palos Verdes Drive North being very narrow which could pose a conflict
  between horses, cyclists and cars.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 26, 2016
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted his opinion that equestrians should cross
  at Palos Verdes Drive North/Crenshaw Boulevard where there is a traffic signal.
  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF commented that this would be out of the way for an
  equestrian.

  Dee Keese, 26750 Eastvale Road, Palos Verdes Peninsula, provided her
  experience in being a long-time resident and commented that an equestrian
  could go over to John’s Trail so there would not be any horses between
  Westfield and No Name Street which she believed would solve the problem.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Tiffany Chiu, Tiffany’s Red Barn,
  explained the location from her barn that goes into the Westfield neighborhood.
  She relayed her experience with the trails in proximity to her barn and that the
  overgrown vegetation is a problem.

  Alan Hoffman, 26672 Eastvale Road, noted his concern that utilizing John’s
  Canyon Trail is not realistic. He further suggested a compromise that would
  include clearing out the vegetation and installing a fence to create a barrier
  between the horses and cyclists.

  Bruce Grimes, 3875 Palos Verdes Drive North, provided a history of his parents’
  residence in the City.

  City Manager Prichard noted that staff could clear the trail to re-establish what
  was there previously and then COUNCIL could make a decision on installation
  of the crossing once the new conditions have been monitored.

  Mark Byrne commented that he lives next door to the proposed crosswalk and
  walks along Palos Verdes Drive North and has to wait a long time to cross the
  street. He further commented that having a path there would be preferable.

  City Manager Prichard noted that in prior years mid-block crossings were
  eliminated and that technology, i.e., in-pavement lights was not the standard.
  He further noted that now equipment is available to provide additional
  warnings. He then suggested that given the history and concerns raised, the
  COUNCIL could direct staff to clear the trail and bring back this item at a
  future meeting.

  Brenda Harpino, Volunteer, Lomita Sheriff’s Posse, noted that even in uniform,
  they will wait a significant amount of time on Palos Verdes Drive North before
  drivers stop to let them cross. She further noted that drivers would not be able
  to see an equestrian as there is a tree where the trail meets Eastvale Road.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE CLEARING OUT THE VEGETATION ON THE SOUTH SIDE
  OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH FROM EASTVALE ROAD TO NO NAME
  STREET IN AN EFFORT TO OBSERVE HOW EQUESTRIANS ACTUALLY
  UTILIZE THIS TRAIL AND BRING BACK THOSE OBSERVATIONS TO THE
  COUNCIL AT A FUTURE MEETING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

C.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF APRIL 6,
  2016: DEEP VALLEY DRIVE AT ROXCOVE DRIVE CROSSWALK – ADDITIONAL
  TRAFFIC CONTROL

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the recommendations as
  listed in the staff report.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Extensive discussion took place regarding the number and placement of signs,
  with the consensus of the COUNCIL being to minimize the number of signs and
  pavement markings while still achieving the goal of clearly identifying the
  crosswalks.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 26, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE RECOMMENDATION AS AMENDED WITHOUT THE
  INSTALLATION OF DOUBLE-SIDED SIGNS AND PAINTED TRAFFIC
  MARKINGS ON THE STREET.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

D.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF APRIL 6,
  2016: PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND SILVER SPUR ROAD – STOP
  CONTROL OPERATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the recommendations as
  listed in the staff report.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material).

  Traffic Engineer Itagaki provided a presentation showing traffic flow at the Palos
  Verdes Drive North/Silver Spur Road intersection before and after the recent
  improvements. She noted that traffic back-up has decreased due to the two
  through lanes on Palos Verdes Drive North at Silver Spur Road. Finally she
  noted that removal of the third merge arrow, relocating the speed limit signs,
  and installing an intersection sign and merge sign have also been proposed.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ stated that she felt the merge lane sign is not
  necessary.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that residents are concerned about the
  number of signs.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO APPROVE THE RECOMMENDATION AS AMENDED WITHOUT THE
  MERGE SYMBOL SIGN.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES – MAYOR AND COUNCIL MEMBERS
  EXECUTIVE FORUM/ADVANCED LEADERSHIP WORKSHOPS SCHEDULED
  FOR JUNE 22-24, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ

  TO AUTHORIZE THOSE COUNCIL MEMBERS WISHING TO ATTEND THIS
  CONFERENCE.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN announced two vacancies on the Park and Activities
  Commission and one vacancy on the Environmental Advisory Committee and
  encouraged anyone who is interested to submit an application.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
APRIL 26, 2016
   ***

  At 9:20 p.m., the CITY COUNCIL convened into closed session.

  ***

14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6)
  Agency Designated Representatives: City Manager
  Employee Organization: City of Rolling Hills Estates Employees’ Association

  DIRECTED STAFF TO CONTINUE NEGOTIATIONS.

B.  DISCUSSION WITH RESPECT TO PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT: QUARTERLY CITY
  MANAGER REVIEW
  (Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957)

  ***

  At 11:05 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened with MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, MAYOR
  PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL
  AND COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ present.

  ***

15.  ADJOURNMENT IN MEMORY OF LONG-TIME PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSIONER DAVID R. PIERSON

  At 11:05 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN formally adjourned the City Council

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
